MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  July 11, 2017

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the
Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor
Bucknum at 5:05 p.m., on July 11, 2017, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on July 6, 2017, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also posted
at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the Norman P.
Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Goodell
  Council Member Raths
  Council Member Kelley
  Mayor Pro Tem Sachs
  Mayor Bucknum

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

CLOSED SESSION

CS1. Conference with Real Property Negotiators. Property: APN 808-720-07, APN 808-
  571-01, APN 808-720-08, APN 808-720-09, APN 808-720-10, APN 808-720-11, APN
  808-720-12, APN 808-132-16. Agency Negotiators: City Manager Wilberg; Assistant
  City Manager Rattay; Community Development Director Lister; Administrative
  Services Director Dyas, City Attorney. Negotiating Parties: NGP Realty. Under
  Negotiation: Price and Terms of Payment.

City Council Minutes  1  July 11, 2017
 RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:05 p.m., Mayor Bucknum recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City
Council reconvened at 6:04 p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that staff received direction from the City Council but no
reportable action occurred.

INVOCATION: Council Member Goodell

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Mayor Pro Tem Sachs

PRESENTATIONS

P1.  Presentation on Chamber Restaurant Week

  The City Council and audience received the presentation from Doug Zielasko, Chamber of
  Commerce Chief Operating Officer.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

"Batgirl" (Genesis Hansen, Director of Library Services): invited the City Council and the
community to the superhero-themed Prelude in the Park and Pacific Symphony which will be held
on July 22, 2017, from 4:30 to 8:00 p.m. on the Village Green at Oso Viejo Community Park.

Julie Collier, representing Congressman Darrell Issa's Office: thanked the City for allowing the
Congressman’s staff to set up mobile office hours at Mission Viejo city hall last week. She also
provided an update on proposed legislation relative to sober living homes.

Mona Amirseyedian and Jason Yi, M.V.: discussed the Community of Character Youth Committee
and announced that the character trait for the month of July is fairness.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Mayor Bucknum, to approve the Consent
Calendar as outlined below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

1.  Waive Reading of Ordinances and Resolutions
City Council Minutes  2  July 11, 2017
   Approved the reading by title of all ordinances and resolutions and declared that said titles
  which appear on the public agenda shall be determined to have been read by title and further
  reading waived.

2.  City Council Minutes

  Approved the Minutes for the regular City Council meeting of June 27, 2017, as presented.

3.  Check Register Dated June 16, 2017 in the Amount of $890,787.68

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

4.  Check Register Dated June 23, 2017 in the Amount of $1,506,440.11

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

5.  Adoption of FY 2017-18 Budget for the Mission Viejo Community Development
  Financing Authority

  Adopted CDFA Resolution 17-01 Adopting a Budget for the Mission Viejo Community
  Development Financing Authority for the 2017-18 Fiscal Year.

6.  Mission Viejo Housing Authority Budget - Fiscal Year 2017-18

  Adopted Housing Authority Resolution 17-02 Adopting a Budget for the Mission Viejo
  Housing Authority (MVHA) for FY 2017-18.

7.  Mission Viejo Community Development  Financing  Authority  (MVCDFA)
  Treasurer’s Monthly Report for May 2017

  Received and filed.

8.  City Treasurer’s Monthly Report for May 2017

  Received and filed.

9.  Mission Viejo Housing Authority (MVHA) Treasurer’s Monthly Report for May
  2017

  Received and filed.

10.  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency Treasurer’s Monthly
  Report for May 2017

  Received and filed.

City Council Minutes  3  July 11, 2017
 11.  Transfer of Southern California Edison Rule 20A Allocations

  Authorized the City Manager to enter into an agreement with the City of Newport Beach
  to transfer the City's unused Rule 20A allocation of $131,762.00 within the Southern
  California Edison (SCE) Service Area to the City of Newport Beach in exchange for
  compensation in the amount of $72,469.10.

12.  Felipe Recreation Center Rehabilitation - Restroom and Office Building - CIP’s
  (307/310)

  (1) Approved the plans and specifications and authorized staff to advertise for bids for the
  Felipe Recreation Center Rehabilitation, Restroom and Office Building - CIPs (307/310)
  and (2) approved Contract Amendment No. 1 to civTEC engineering consultant, in an
  amount not to exceed $1,250.00 for additional survey.

13.  Cordova Park Play Area and Lighting Renovations - CIPs 306 & 309

  Approved the plans and specifications and authorized staff to advertise for bids for the
  Cordova Park Play Area & Lighting Renovations – CIP’s (306 & 309).

14.  Purchase of replacement furniture for the Norman P. Murray Community and Senior
  Center and the Mission Viejo Library.

  (1) Awarded a contract to Yamada Enterprises in an amount not to exceed $116,422.88 for
  the purchase of replacement chairs at the Norman P. Murray Community and Senior Center
  and issue a purchase order; and (2) awarded a contract to Yamada Enterprises in an amount
  not to exceed $123,507.55 for the purchase and installation of various replacement
  furniture at the Mission Viejo Library and issue a purchase order.

15.  2017 Residential Resurfacing (CIP 18838)-Slurry Seal

  Approved the bid specifications, subject to minor revisions required by the City Engineer,
  and authorized staff to advertise for construction bids for the subject project.

16.  Potocki Center Name Change

  Approved recommended name change from "Thomas R. Potocki Conference Center" to
  "Thomas R. Potocki Center for the Arts."

17.  Agreement with Pacific Symphony for Symphony in the Cities

  Approved agreement with Pacific Symphony for Symphony in the Cities.

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

City Council Minutes  4  July 11, 2017
 OLD BUSINESS

18.  Electing To Be Subject To California Government Code Section 20516 By Contract
  Amendment With The California Public Employees’ Retirement System

  Director of Administrative Services Cheryl Dyas presented the staff report.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Sachs, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to adopt
  Resolution 17-33 Electing to be Subject to California Government Code Section 20516 by
  Contract Amendment with the California Public Employees' Retirement System and
  Satisfaction of All Requirements Thereto.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS

19.  Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Report

  Mayor Pro Tem Sachs presented the report.

20.  Voting Delegate and Alternate(s) for the 2017 League of California Cities Annual
  Conference

  Mayor Bucknum appointed Mayor Pro Tem Sachs as the Voting Delegate and herself and
  Council Member Kelley as Alternates for the League of California Cities Conference
  Annual Business Meeting on September 15, 2017.

21.  Community Services Commission Vacancy and Appointment

  Mayor Bucknum noted that Commissioner Judy Bullockus is now serving on the
  Capistrano Unified School District Board of Directors and she will be missed at the City.

  Motion made by Mayor Bucknum, seconded by Council Member Goodell, to appoint
  Cameron Knauerhaze to the Community Services Commission.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

City Council Minutes  5  July 11, 2017
 STAFF REPORTS

22.  Orange County Sheriff’s Department (OCSD) Update

  Lt. Ken Binning presented a report on recent activity in the area of public safety including
  the graduation of 24 new deputies from the Orange County Sheriff’s Regional Training
  Academy; Coffee with a Cop at the Starbucks on La Paz with at least 25 citizens in
  attendance; National Take Back day where over 375 lbs. of expired or unwanted
  prescription drugs were collected; the local, state and national Peace Officers Memorial
  ceremonies; and the 1st OCSD Special Recognition Ceremony where a Mission Viejo
  deputy was honored.

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

23.  Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended

  By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities
  calendars as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk
  for the public record.

City Manager’s Report

City Manager Dennis Wilberg discussed Assembly Bill (AB) 1000 which started out as a simple
bill dealing with water meters however, every reference to water meters was gutted out. The bill
now creates opposition to the Cadiz Water Project which is sponsored by Santa Margarita Water
District and has already gone through the environmental approval process. He said the Water
District has asked the City to send a letter of opposition to the State, which staff is drafting for the
Mayor’s signature. Mr. Wilberg also noted that the City’s Legislative Affairs consultant,
Townsend Public Affairs, attended hearings in Sacramento and expressed Mission Viejo’s
opposition to AB1000.

Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services Keith Rattay presented an update on the
Marguerite Aquatics Complex rehabilitation project.

Council Member Goodell

Council Member Goodell announced that he has been attending some of the Nadadores Master
Swim workouts and he is very excited about what is happening with the team. He said it's always
fun for him to go back and spend time with the Nadadores. Council Member Goodell discussed
his attendance at the League of California Cities executive training for Mayors and City Council
Members. He said that based on conversations he heard, Mission Viejo is doing very well
financially and many other cities are in bad shape and concerned about the future. Council Member
Goodell noted that there is important work ahead and the City needs to look at other ways it can
support business development and revenues. He said he takes his role as a Council Member very
seriously and he felt that League training session was valuable.

City Council Minutes  6  July 11, 2017
 Council Member Kelley

Council Member Kelley expressed her appreciation to the Mission Viejo Activities Committee
(MVAC) for another exceptional 4th of July Street Faire and she thanked longtime member Cathy
Allen for an outstanding job as the Chair of the event. Council Member Kelley wondered if all the
attendees who come out to enjoy the festivities know that such a small handful of people organize
this annual community event. She announced that the Mission Viejo Marine Adoption Committee
Boots, Beer and BBQ event will be held July 16 at the Norman P. Murray Community Center from
4:00 to 7:00 p.m. Tickets are $25 per person and can be purchased at the community center. All
proceeds will benefit the City’s adopted Marine Battalion, the food will be catered by Outback
Steakhouse, and there will be a live DJ and line dance lessons. Council Member Kelley also
reminded residents that Pacific Symphony will play at Oso Viejo Park on July 22 with the Prelude
in the Park preceding the concert at 4:00 p.m. There will be a superhero theme and children are
encouraged to wear their superhero costumes. She thanked the student members of the Character
Committee who spoke earlier in the meeting about the Committee and she outlined the monthly
character word program and the materials that are distributed to local schools. This month’s
character movie is “Hidden Figures” which will be shown at 2:00 p.m. on Sunday, July 16 at the
Norman P. Murray Community Center. Council Member Kelley said the Committee is always
looking for new members and those interested can get more information from her or staff member
Vickie Sullivan at the library. In closing, Council Member Kelley read a quote about fairness from
Michael Josephson: “A person of character plays fair even when others don't and values no
achievement unless it was attained with honor.”

Council Member Raths

Council Member Raths welcomed the new Community Services Commissioner Cameron
Knauerhaze and thanked Chamber of Commerce Chief Operating Officer Doug Zielasko for his
presentation earlier this evening. Council Member Raths said he is excited about the Chamber’s
upcoming Restaurant Week and Buy Local campaign and he wished everyone a good summer.

Mayor Pro Tem Sachs

Mayor Pro Tem Sachs announced that he received word that there is a 25 to 30 acre fire at Camp
Pendleton, just yards from where the last fire burned. He noted that the Orange County Fire
Authority personnel are stretched thin so he wished them all the best. Mayor Pro Tem Sachs
commented on the State Legislature’s bills and propositions which are adding crime to the streets
and getting folks kicked out of sober living homes. He said he has been made aware of three new
bills that he finds disgusting: SB620 would will allow a judge to decide if they want to dismiss the
firearms sentencing enhancement; SB10 would eliminate the fixed bill structure to allow felons
pre-trial release; and SB421 would allow for the Megan’s Law prescribed sentencing period to be
lifted. Mayor Pro Tem Sachs said that once again, California’s legislators are leading the state in
the wrong direction and their actions are percolating down to the cities. He suggested that residents
write to their senators and let them know how offensive it is that these bills are even being
discussed.

City Council Minutes  7  July 11, 2017
 Mayor Bucknum

Mayor Bucknum thanked Mayor Pro Tem Sachs for his comments and noted that there are people
all over the country who are up in arms over various things but the bills that Mr. Sachs mentioned
should be the focus of Californians’ anger and activism. She said that these bills put families and
police officers in jeopardy and would protect criminals. Mayor Bucknum discussed upcoming
events including the opening of a photography exhibit at the Mission Viejo Library on July 14 at
7:00 p.m.; a Family Luau at Montanoso Recreation Center on July 15 from 4:00 to 9:00 p.m.; the
Pacific Symphony on July 21 and a Concert on the Green on July 20 with the band Family Style.
She announced that the Trabuco Hills High School Marching Band participated in the National
Parade and she has been asked to nominate up to 3 high schools for next year’s parade. Mayor
Bucknum invited residents to her “Walk with Wendy” mobile town hall meeting on August 5. She
will meet residents at 8:00 a.m. near the bocce courts outside the community center before
proceeding to walk along the Oso Creek Trail.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 7:23 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Bucknum adjourned the meeting to Tuesday, August 22, 2017, at 5:00 p.m.

____________________________________
Karen Hamman, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of August 22, 2017

City Council Minutes  8  July 11, 2017
